text:
sophia: Quick async check — I kicked off a cross-variant perf pass for the qpref experiment (job qp-2187) comparing int4 vs fp8 on two production traces (search-heavy + longform). Can folks help triage quality vs latency tradeoffs? PR: https://git.redwood/infra/quant-qpref (WIP)
omar: Ack. Can you paste the exact benchmark commands + seed so I can reproduce locally? Also, what's the gating threshold for acceptance? :thinking_face:
sophia: Command is:
```
./bench/run --job qp-2187 --variant int4 --trace search_traces_v2 --seed 42 --seq-len-dist=prod
```
and same with `--variant fp8`. Gating: target <=1.5% relative drop in quality for int4, <=0.5% for fp8 vs baseline fp16, AND tail p99 latency within 10% of baseline.
kai: I'll run the profiler and attach traces. Heads-up: last run I saw a KV-cache warmup tail at ~1.2s for longform which affected p99. Will capture `perfproto` traces.
perf-bot: started job qp-2187-int4 on cluster-gpu-5 — logs: https://ci.redwood/jobs/qp-2187-int4/logs — ETA ~25m :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ci-bot: PR pipeline passed for quant-qpref branch (unit, lint). Integration tests pending.
rebecca: Quick data note — for dataset_x (customer-style queries) int4 previously showed a 2.1% BLEU-like drop in earlier sweep. I'll run targeted eval slices (rare tokens, long-context) and share diffs.
omar: When you say 'relative drop', which metric exactly? BLEU/ROUGE/accuracy? We need a single number for automation.
sophia: Use F1 on our canonical promptset (qpref-f1) as the primary metric. Secondary: token-level hallucination rate. I pushed the eval config to the PR.
kai: Profiling update: suspected hotspot in fused-attn kernel when seq_len>1024. Patch suggestion: fall back to non-fused for warmup then switch. Command I used to capture trace:
```
PYTHONWARNINGS=ignore python infra/profiler.py --job qp-2187 --out /tmp/qp-2187-trace --kv-warmup 64
```
rebecca: Eval results (first pass): int4 vs fp16 on qpref-f1: -1.8% int4, -0.4% fp8. Hallucination delta: +0.6% int4, +0.1% fp8. Full diffs: https://artifacts.redwood/evals/qp-2187/diffs
omar: Hmm int4 is slightly past the gating (1.8% > 1.5%). Any obvious prompt slices causing most of the drop?
sophia: From quick look, losses concentrated on long-context Q+A and rare-token named entities. We should try prioritized kv-warmup + micro-batching tweak and re-run int4.
kai: Agreed — I can test a microbatch size change and force KV pre-warm on the first request. Quick patch:
```
- microbatch=8
+ microbatch=4
+ ENV: KV_PREWARM=1
```
I'll run the job with that.
perf-bot: started job qp-2187-int4-prewarm (patch-kv) — logs: https://ci.redwood/jobs/qp-2187-int4-prewarm/logs
rebecca: Running eval on the prewarm run now. If it stays under 1.5% and p99 holds, we can mark int4 as acceptable for the canary.
omar: Also FYI saw a small latency regression with fp8 on short sequences (~3% regression). Not sure if noise. Anyone seeing consistent pattern?
kai: That matches my kernel sampling — fp8 codepath has an extra quant-dequant step for short sequences that dominates. Possible micro-optimization: skip quant-dequant for <64 tokens.
sophia: Good catch. For canary decision: prioritize keeping customer-facing short-seq latency tight. If fp8 harms short-seq, we should route short-seq to fp16 until we optimize.
rebecca: Prewarm run eval: int4 now -1.3% qpref-f1, hallucination +0.4%, p99 latency ~+6% (baseline). This should meet our gating if we accept p99 within 10%.
omar: Sounds reasonable. Two asks: (1) can we snapshot the exact model weights/commit for the canary pin, (2) add a canary config to route 5% traffic to int4 with quick rollback.
sophia: I'll pin the model: commit sha `a7f9c3e`. Canary config: will add route `quant:int4 -> 5% canary` with automatic fallback to fp16 on error or >1.2% quality regression.
kai: PR update: added KV_PREWARM env + microbatch change, included profiler trace and flamegraph. PTAL @omar @rebecca
omar: Quick code review: LGTM modulo a small docstring nit. One question: default KV_PREWARM=0 for older clusters? Should be opt-in.
rebecca: Approving once CI passes. I'll also add the eval slices to the rollout checklist.
ci-bot: Canary deploy job started: https://ci.redwood/deploys/qp-2187-canary — monitoring hooks active (quality/slo dashboards)
perf-bot: canary traffic sample: 5k requests so far, int4 signal shows F1 delta -1.2% rolling, tail p99 +5.5% — continuing to monitor.
sophia: Nicely coordinated — next steps: (1) let canary run for 24h, (2) kai to experiment on skipping fp8 quant-dequant for short seqs, (3) rebecca to update rollout checklist and add exact eval thresholds, (4) omar to merge PR after CI + doc nit fix. Thanks all. :trophy:
omar: Will merge after CI green and doc fix. Thanks.
kai: I'll post profiler notes in the PR and open a follow-up ticket for fp8 short-seq micro-opt.
rebecca: Adding retrospective note to the quant board about dataset_x sensitivity.
sophia: Closing the async thread — ping here if anything regresses.
